final_candidates.decision_summary: D473 in TM10 provides the essential negative electrostatic charge required for coordinating organic cations; replacing it with alanine completely eliminates substrate transport while preserving overall folding and membrane trafficking.
D473N neutralizes the critical negative charge while preserving side-chain volume and polarity, selectively inactivating organic cation translocation with minimal structural disruption.

W216 forms the core aromatic cation-pi interaction site within the substrate translocation cavity; alanine substitution severely impairs substrate binding and transport without destabilizing the transporter structure.

stop_reason.detail: Optimal candidates targeting the primary substrate-binding pocket with known transport inactivation and preserved folding have been established.

history.rationale: D473 is the canonical substrate-binding carboxylate in TM11; neutralizing it abolishes organic cation transport without perturbing membrane expression or folding.

D473 provides the essential negative electrostatic charge in TM10 required for organic cation coordination; its alanine substitution completely abolishes transport while preserving folding and membrane localization.
Isosteric substitution of the essential TM11 acidic residue removes the negative charge required for cation binding while maintaining local side-chain packing.
D473N neutralizes the essential charge while maintaining steric volume and polarity, selectively eliminating cation transport with minimal risk of structural perturbation.
R171 is the core basic residue of the conserved MFS motif A between TM2 and TM3; mutating it disrupts alternating-access conformational switching, abolishing transport.
R171 plays a role in the conformational gating network, where disruption blocks the transport cycle.
R398 participates in the C-terminal MFS motif A network in the TM8-TM9 loop, where alanine substitution blocks rocker-switch mechanics while retaining native fold.
R398 is part of the intracellular gating/salt-bridge network, impairing transport when mutated.
D397 acts as the acidic partner in the cytoplasmic motif A charge relay, and its removal arrests transporter turnover without destabilizing the scaffold.
D397 pairs with intracellular basic residues; alanine substitution blocks rocker-switch conformational transition.
W216 provides a critical cation-pi interaction in the central translocation pore; alanine substitution impairs substrate recognition while preserving helical structure.
W216 is a critical aromatic residue in TM4 mediating cation-pi interactions with substrates; mutating it disrupts transport activity while maintaining transporter trafficking.
E385 lies in the central permeation pathway in TM8; neutralization impedes substrate translocation while preserving transmembrane alpha-helical bundle integrity.
E385 in TM7 contributes to cavity electrostatics, though its transport defect is slightly milder than TM10 D473.
Gln substitution preserves side-chain volume and hydrogen-bonding potential of E385 while eliminating the negative charge needed for cation transport.
E385Q preserves side-chain volume while removing charge, impairing transport with high expression retention.
Neutralizes the motif A positive charge while retaining polar contacts, halting rocker-switch transport cycles with minimal perturbation to expression.
R171Q eliminates the positively charged guanidinium group required for substrate translocation dynamics.
F243 is a central cavity aromatic residue participating in hydrophobic substrate coordination; mutating to Ala disables transport while maintaining stable folding.
F243 forms part of the hydrophobic ceiling of the substrate cavity, weakening substrate binding when substituted.
